source.title: Ventriloquist LLMs: Linear Alignment of Late-Stage Representations

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some tables and figures are flattened in the web extraction, but the results used below are identifiable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests cross-model representation compatibility and linear interchangeability using affine maps, CKA/SVCCA, and downstream task evaluations; it does not reproduce the original Platonic-claim method as a scaling study.
record.gate_note: The paper directly measures representation similarity and tests linear mapping of representations into another model’s fixed head. Reported CKA/SVCCA findings and task-transfer outcomes are included where they bear on the claim. Results cited from other work are excluded. Many task-supervised classification, OOD-detection, and distribution-mismatched alignment results are not included because the 60-row limit is reached; see rows_left_out.
record.test_reason: The study fits affine maps between the final hidden states of independently trained LLMs and embedding models (different vendors, architectures and data). It then measures how much downstream classification, MMLU and generation quality survives through the target's frozen head. This directly tests V4. It also bears on V7 (incomplete, tokenizer-dependent, late-layer-only compatibility) and, loosely, on V1 (source scale threshold). It is not a controlled scaling replication of the Platonic method.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Authors conclude that affine maps between final hidden states preserve classification and OOD performance and sometimes enable generation. Success depends on tokenizer overlap and source scale; the stated threshold varies in the text (≤1B, <2B, below 4B). Transfer is asymmetric strong-to-weak. Compatibility is localized to the last 1–2 layers, an output-space phenomenon rather than shared reasoning. They add that maps fit on unrelated data transfer, suggesting a task-independent relation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses affine alignment of final hidden states, linear CKA/SVCCA, and downstream classification, OOD, and generation tests; it is not a controlled scaling study of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis.
record.method_sensitivity: Generation quality varies with tokenizer overlap, source-model scale, mapping direction, model pair, and layer depth. The paper reports token match rate and Jaccard correlations with quality.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear transfer is direction-asymmetric. Strong-to-weak maps beat weak-to-strong, and the same pair can score 4.13 versus 1.86 depending on direction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-model linear compatibility is limited by the source model's capacity rather than being a symmetric similarity.

fits_no_version.finding: Exact token-match rate (r=0.898) and vocabulary Jaccard (r=0.822) predict generation quality across 23 ≥4B pairs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shared tokenization, a training design choice, governs output-space linear compatibility of LLMs.

record.problems: Model pairs are heterogeneous rather than a controlled scale series; generation evaluation uses 100 Alpaca prompts and 100 MMLU questions. Some reported generation evaluations have small samples. The paper reports some uncertainty and repeated runs for similarity measures, but many table entries have no uncertainty estimates. The web-extracted tables are flattened.
record.rows_left_out: To stay within 60 rows, omitted four DBpedia classification rows from Section 3.1 Table 1, all OOD AUROC entries in that table, and the separate distribution-mismatched-data classification results in Section 5 and Appendix A.3. The paper states that task-supervised alignment largely preserves classification and that OOD-only maps recover strong accuracy, but those individual table results are not recorded here.

untested.parts: No controlled scaling sweep. There is no measure of similarity rising with size or capability across architectures or objectives; only a source-size threshold is shown in heterogeneous pairs, confounded with tokenizer.
No vision-language or paired image-caption data.
No relative representations, no fully unpaired mapping, and no standard mid-network stitching with the remaining target layers run.
No neuron, SAE-feature or circuit universality.
No systematic variation of similarity metric or its settings. The alignment-data shift in Section 5 concerns the map's fitting data, not the similarity measure.
Does not test whether shared training data or objectives, rather than a shared world model, explain alignment, beyond the tokenizer-overlap correlation.

missing.what: Tokenizer overlap versus judge score correlations: exact match r=0.898, Jaccard r=0.822, n=23; high-quality pairs have exact match ≥0.67
CKA among instruction-tuned LLMs on Alpaca and TriviaQA. Gemma-270M and Qwen3-30B are lower (about 0.48–0.73); Llama-1B↔Llama-8B reaches 0.886

Task-supervised MNLI losses: OpenAI target ← Qwen 87.9→61.3, Mistral ← Qwen 87.9→78.5, Cohere ← Gemini 65.0→56.8; IMDB OOD AUROC drops (0.905→0.693). rows_left_out mislabels Appendix A.3 as distribution-mismatched
Maps fit on OOD generic text recover most accuracy, e.g. AG News 79.6–84.4 versus full-data 92–93; MNLI Gemini←OpenAI 33.5 versus 65.0
Human scores: high-quality cross-model pairs 3.0 versus large native 4.5; perplexity degradation 26% for 7–8B pairs versus 37% for small-to-large

record.verdict_notes: Many rows had wrong pairs; values were mostly right. Table 5's flattened columns were misread for the low-quality block, Table 1 source and target were mixed up, and Table 2 swapped Llama and Qwen natives. Row states are scored against V4; for V7, absent transfer counts as evidence for it. Table 3's direction labels (Qwen→Llama 0.70) conflict with Table 2 (Qwen→Llama 68, Llama→Qwen 48), so L-row direction is uncertain. The layer sweep's machine-epsilon residual with about 1.55M token pairs, and whether intermediate target states are decoded without the remaining layers, are unclear. This may make L01–L06 a weak test of stitching. The study cites the Platonic paper but is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Tests whether source-model scale affects success of linear cross-model generation, but does not conduct a controlled scaling sweep or establish that representation similarity rises monotonically with model size and capability across different architectures, objectives, data, or modalities.
No paired image-caption or other vision-language representation alignment test.
No comparison of models trained from different random seeds of the same architecture.

Tests affine maps at final/late hidden states and transfer through fixed heads; does not test stitching intermediate layers of different architectures beyond the reported depth sweep, relative representations, or unpaired-data mapping.
No recurring interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits are tested.
Uses multiple similarity measures and datasets, but does not systematically test whether changing metric settings or inputs causes convergence to weaken or vanish.
Shows incomplete and condition-dependent transfer, but does not test whether shared training data or objectives explain alignment instead of a common model of reality.

source_check.condition: Alpaca generation with small (<2B) versus ≥4B sources, including same-family perfect-tokenizer pairs
source_check.reason: These comparisons establish a source-capacity dependence of fitted generation interfaces, not increasing representational alignment as independently trained models become larger and more capable. They test V4 rather than V1.

relationships.condition: MMLU transfer in both directions between large and small models
relationships.reason: The scale effect is a source-capacity threshold and is asymmetric, not mutual convergence. Large sources decode well through a 270M head (M04 49, M06 68), while 270M sources sit at chance (M03, M05).
relationships.display_finding: Large sources achieve MMLU scores of 49 and 68 through a 270M head, while 270M sources remain at chance, indicating an asymmetric source-capacity threshold.

relationships.condition: All tested LLM pairs and depths
relationships.reason: Compatibility is incomplete: CKA is 0.595–0.881 (C01) and generation retains 60–70% (P01–P11). It is tokenizer-dependent (P12–P18; r=0.898 from text) and confined to the last 1–2 layers (L01–L12). Authors read it as output-space geometry, not shared reasoning.
relationships.display_finding: CKA was 0.595–0.881 and generation retained 60–70%, with compatibility confined to the last 1–2 layers and strongly tokenizer-dependent (r = 0.898); the authors interpreted this as output-space geometry rather than shared reasoning.

source_check.notes:
Source is arXiv v6. Table 2 and Table 3 give different final-transfer accuracies; the main text names GPT-5.1 as judge while Appendix B names GPT-5.2.
The 60–70% retention is the authors' aggregate characterization, not a reported ratio for every pair; generic large-model baselines are not exact paired baselines.

statements.correction: Table 5: Qwen14B → Mistral-Nemo 1.86; reverse 4.13; small-source generation 1.00–1.83. Table 2: Gemma270M → Llama8B 20 and → Qwen7B 21, native 22; Llama1B → Llama8B 36 and → Qwen7B 28, native 42; four-choice chance 25.
statements.problem: Chance-level MMLU transfer is overgeneralized to all sources below 2B; the tested 1B source scores above chance in both directions.
